analyst_view.overall: Cologne (14th, 10 points, no win in five) host promoted Elversberg (9th, 13 points), who play an open, attacking game and have conceded 11 in their last five. Cologne's injury list is long (Dallinga, Skhiri, Hübers, Rav van den Berg, Rondic and Castro-Montes), and the numbers count all of these, taking roughly a fifth off Cologne's goals. Captain and goalkeeper Marvin Schwäbe still has back trouble and a test on Friday decides whether he plays; coach René Wagner says Ron-Robert Zieler is ready, and striker Ragnar Ache is fit but unlikely to start. Elversberg news is thin; the expected line-up has Pinckert and Gyamerah back in defence. Referee Sören Storks (4.8 cards a game) is now in the numbers, and I found nothing they can't see that points one way, so I stay with them on every stat.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.5 goals and already take Cologne's absentees off, mainly Dallinga (about -11%), Skhiri and Castro-Montes. Elversberg's open defence suits Cologne's breakers El Mala, Maina and Moore, while a possible switch from Schwäbe to Zieler in goal is only a doubt and Ache is likely on the bench, so these pull both ways and I stay at 2.5.

corners.text: The numbers say 11.1 corners, most of them Cologne's (7.1), and already count both teams' recent corner form. Cologne often attack on the break, which can mean fewer corners than that split suggests, but Elversberg concede plenty of corners (43 in six), so nothing new moves me from 11.1.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.9 cards; they already add about 25% for referee Sören Storks (4.8 cards a game) and some for both teams' recent bookings (Cologne 16 in six). This is not a derby or a heated fixture, so with the referee already counted I stay at 4.9.

shots.text: The numbers say 28.1 shots and already trim a few for Cologne's quieter recent attacking. Elversberg's open style should give Cologne room to shoot on the break, and Elversberg like to have the ball, which is how both teams usually play, so I stay at 28.1.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 8.8 shots on target and already reflect Cologne's recent attacking without Dallinga. Ache's return gives Cologne a proper centre-forward option off the bench, but nothing new changes the picture either way, so I stay at 8.8.
